findings.description: The `-c` overrides turn off `log.showSignature` and `merge.verifySignatures`, but a session-set `rebase.instructionFormat` containing `%G?` still verifies every rebased commit with the planted `gpg.program`, outside the sandbox.
findings.body:
[`GIT_SAFE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/427beb6a2518346d15c45e88ba0b3c284c85c686/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L44-L57) now turns off `log.showSignature` and `merge.verifySignatures`. The gate's own path has a third way to trigger signature verification: `rebase.instructionFormat`.

Why it fires:
- A non-interactive `git rebase <target>` on the default merge backend (git ≥ 2.26, which includes the Apple Git 2.39.5 decision 79 cites) still builds its todo list through `sequencer_make_script`.
- That function reads `rebase.instructionFormat` from config. It falls back to `%s` only when the key is unset or empty, and pretty-prints every commit it will pick with that format.
- A `%G?` in the format calls `check_commit_signature`, which runs `gpg.program` on any commit that carries a `gpgsig` header. This is the forged-header trick decision 79 describes, and `log.showSignature` has no effect on it.

How a session gets there:
1. It sets `rebase.instructionFormat=%G?%s` (or `pretty.foo=%G?` together with `instructionFormat=foo`) and `gpg.program=<payload>` in the shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config`.
2. It commits a forged `gpgsig` object with `git hash-object`.
3. It bases its work so the target is not an ancestor.
4. `pup merge` then runs [`runGit(worktree, ['rebase', target])`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/427beb6a2518346d15c45e88ba0b3c284c85c686/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L340-L345). Per the comment at L211-216, that call runs with the operator's environment, before the sandbox. The payload runs once per replayed commit.

`assertNoArmedGitDrivers` matches only filter and merge drivers, so neither key is refused. `instructionFormat` appears nowhere in the decisions.

The fix is to pin the key at command scope, the same way as the others. `%s` contains `%`, so git uses it as a literal format and never looks up a `pretty.<alias>`, which closes the alias variant too. Please also:
- name the key in the JSDoc above `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` and in decision 79;
- extend the forged-signature test with a control case where plain `git rebase` fires the program and `runGit(..., ['rebase', target])` does not.

This is medium confidence: the git-internals claim comes from reading sequencer source, not from a run under CI's static review.

findings.description: The new spaced-path `describe` was inserted between the decision-41 `diff.external`/textconv comment (L79-82) and the armed-diff-driver `describe` it documents (now L111). That comment now heads the wrong suite and runs into the new `-z` line. Move the decision-41 comment back above L111.

The `gitDiffNumstat` assertion would also pass on the pre-PR code. Every `--numstat -z` record starts with a digit or `-`, and the output ends in `\0`, which `trim()` does not strip. So only the `gitDiffPaths` and `gitDiffAddedLines` assertions guard the trim fix.

process_issues.description: The conventions reviewer reported that the injected .claude/rules files contained only @-references to docs/conventions/*.md, with no inlined content. It fell back to reading testing.md and the general.md Comments section through Bash, and did not read naming.md.
